comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
This issue was introduced because `_check_queue` tries to filter out queue counter with regex: https://github.com/Azure/sonic-mgmt/blob/1b53581d1d32239a5b133b8c9000c0911746e698/tests/common/dualtor/tunnel_traffic_utils.py#L120-L127
```python
            """ 
            regex search will look for following pattern in queue_counter outpute
            ----------------------------------------------------------------------------_---
            Port           TxQ    Counter/pkts     Counter/bytes     Drop/pkts    Drop/bytes
            -----------  -----  --------------  ---------------  -----------  --------------
            Ethernet124    UC1              10             1000            0             0
            """
            result = re.search(r'\S+\s+UC\d\s+10+\s+\S+\s+\S+\s+\S+', queue_counter)
```
There are several issues with this:
1. Not all `tunnel_traffic_utility` users will send exactly 10 packets to fit this regex.
2. There is no counter clear step before sending the packet and the counter returned by `show queue counter` might be larger than the actual packets sent.
3. there might exist other queues that have 10 as the counter value, for the following example, `Ethernet32:1` is the target queue to match, but `Ethernet24:7` has the same queue counter value as 10, which will error `_check_queue`. 

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
`test_orchagent_slb` failed due to the unmatched queue counter check, this is due to that there might exist other queues that have 10 packets the same as the expected queue.

Signed-off-by: Longxiang Lyu <lolv@microsoft.com>

#### How did you do it?
1. let `_check_queue` use `re.findall` to search all queues that has 10 packets.
2. clear queue counters when entering `tunnel_traffic_monitor`
